sentences.text:
4. Sri Pramod Kumar Singh is present on behalf of Union of India and Sri Raj Kumar Tiwari,
Standing Counsel, on behalf of respondent nos. 3 and 4.
5.

The petitioner has prayed for a mandamus commanding the respondents to pay compensation to her in respect of Gata No. 253, area 0.1780 hectare, village Udaitapur, Tehsil and District Kannauj by calculating the compensation treating the property to be a commercial property.

6. It transpires from the material placed on record that the land of the petitioner was notified for acquisition under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 followed by an award by the Competent Authority dated 21.10.2018.
Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner applied for arbitration under Section 3G(5) of the Act.
The arbitrator decided the matter on 15.9.2021.
The petitioner challenged the arbitrator's award by filing objection under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

The objection was rejected by the Additional District Judge, Court No.- 8,
Kanpur Nagar by order dated 25.1.2023.

entities.text:
Additional District Judge, Court No.- 8,
Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. Section 3G(6) makes applicable the provision of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to every arbitration made under the National Highways Act, 1956.

8. Consequently, the petitioner has right to file appeal under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 against the order of the Court rejecting objection under Section 34.
9.
Instead of availing the said remedy, the petitioner has prayed for a mandamus as noted above.

10. Since, a statutory remedy is available to the petitioner to challenge the order dated 25.1.2023,
but which has not been availed, therefore, no good ground is made out to entertain the instant writ petition.
11. It is, accordingly, dismissed with liberty to the petitioner to avail the remedy of appeal, if so advised.

(Donadi Ramesh, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
